root_cause.text: The dummy-hcd UDC driver emulated synchronize_irq() in the wrong place/order—waiting for callback completion in dummy_pullup() before actually disabling emulated interrupts in dummy_udc_async_callbacks(), allowing new callbacks to start during gadget unbind.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the callback_usage wait loop from dummy_pullup() and moves it into dummy_udc_async_callbacks() immediately after `dum->ints_enabled = enable` when disabling callbacks, while the commit message explicitly states “the emulated synchronize_irq() occurs before the emulated interrupt-disable” and that this “means that more emulated interrupts can occur after the synchronize_irq() emulation has run, leading to the possibility that a callback handler may be running when the gadget driver is unbound.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the callback_usage wait loop from dummy_pullup() so pullup disable no longer blocks waiting for in-flight callbacks to complete.
intent_record.what: The change removes the entire conditional block inside dummy_pullup() that, when value was 0, repeatedly released and reacquired dum->lock and slept in a loop until dum->callback_usage dropped to 0.
intent_record.how: At runtime, disabling pullup no longer waits for outstanding gadget callbacks to finish before returning; the function now only updates dum->pullup, calls set_link_state(), releases the lock, and continues immediately, eliminating the synchronize_irq()-style delay during disconnect handling.

intent_record.intent_summary: Wait for outstanding dummy UDC callbacks to finish when disabling async callbacks to prevent unbind-time races.
intent_record.what: In dummy_udc_async_callbacks(), after setting dum->ints_enabled = enable under dum->lock, the change adds a conditional block for the !enable case that loops while dum->callback_usage > 0, temporarily releases the spinlock with spin_unlock_irq(), sleeps with usleep_range(1000, 2000), then reacquires the lock with spin_lock_irq() until no callbacks remain, before the final spin_unlock_irq().
intent_record.how: When asynchronous callbacks are being disabled, the function now waits for any in-progress callback activity to complete before returning. This prevents unbind or shutdown paths from proceeding while emulated interrupt callbacks are still running, aligning behavior with synchronize_irq()-style serialization and avoiding races with active callbacks.

In `dummy_pullup()`, when `value == 0`, the code now waits for in-flight callbacks before unbind can proceed: `while (dum->callback_usage > 0) { ... usleep_range(1000, 2000); ... }`, with the added comment explicitly stating this is to emulate `synchronize_irq()` before unbind and that doing it in `dummy_udc_stop()` would be too late.
